messages:
ashley: quick Q — we're planning to unpin the hosted default model in next deploy. two things I want to confirm quickly: 1) if a client omits Accept-Model, what exact behavior will they see once 'default' is unpinned? 2) what observability signals should we add to Console so product/CS can detect clients that break due to response-shape changes? cc @ben @maria

ben: short answer first: if Accept-Model is missing we fall back to the default-selection policy (region + tier + pinned overrides). if default is unpinned we resolve to the highest-compat model variant we have available. when fallback capacity is exhausted runtime will surface 429 with X-RW-Circuit header and reason. we should standardize header names. :+1:

ashley: can you paste the exact header names/payload we plan to return? I want to call that out in the deprecation comms so SDKs can watch for it.

ben: example (pseudo):

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RW-Circuit: capacity_exhausted
X-RW-Fallback-To: redwood/gpt-3.2-compat
{
  "error": "capacity_exhausted",
  "message": "No healthy fallback for implicit default. See docs for Accept-Model header."
}
```

ben: also plan to include X-RW-Model-Version when we respond successfully so clients can log mismatches.

maria: product note — for deprecation comms we need: 1) timeline (scheduled unpin date + grace window), 2) example error and recovery steps for integrators, 3) a short FAQ for common SDKs. we should add a Console alert when client_model_mismatch_rate > 0.5% for 1h (so CS can triage).

sam: engineering followups:
- runtime: emit metric rw_model_mismatch_count and tag by route + client_key.
- console: surface a per-route "implicit-default-mismatch" chart and alert.
- sdk: add automatic warning on see X-RW-Model-Version mismatch vs pinned expectation.
I'll put up quick PRs for runtime + metrics.

ashley: regarding response-shape changes — can we send a warning header on successful responses when shape differs from previous model? even if we don't block, that helps detect silent breakages.

ben: we could add X-RW-Response-Shape-Hash for the model+schema version; runtime can compute a simple fingerprint of top-level fields. cheap and useful.

maria: add to FAQ: "If you see new fields, we recommend pinning Accept-Model to the previous model or update your deserializer to tolerate unknown fields."

deploy-bot: [canary] deploy redwood/infra#3408 to us-east-1 completed (canary=2 nodes) — runtime image includes X-RW headers for feature-flag rollout.

ashley: perfect timing — @sam @ben can you two coordinate a short doc (1 pager) in the runbook: what to monitor, what SDKs should do, and rollback steps? I'll loop in CS for comms draft once that's done.

ben: will open CR and doc now — CR #4231, doc: /docs/runbooks/unpin-default-model.md (first draft).

sam: I'll add metrics and the Response-Shape-Hash. ETA for PRs: today EOD.

maria: I'll draft the comms + FAQ and share by tomorrow morning.

ashley: thanks all. quick checklist:
- sam: metrics + header (EOD)
- ben: CR + runbook (in flight)
- maria: comms + FAQ (tomorrow)
- ashley: coordinate CS & legal review (once draft)

ashley: ping me here when the PRs are up so I can link them in the comms. :pray:

ben: pinged — CR: https://phabricator.redwood/4231 (adds X-RW headers + 429 response shape).

sam: runtime PR: https://phabricator.redwood/4242 (metrics + shape hash).

ashley: got both, assigning follow-ups in the runbook. thanks team! :tada:
